This scan is performed and reported by NM Medical
Technique: CT pulmonary angiography with intravenous contrast.
Central filling defect seen within medial basal segmental branches of right lower lobe
artery almost completely occluding its lumen. Eccentric filling defect seen within
medial basal segmental branch of left lower lobe artery.
Areas of subpleural interlobular septal thickening and surrounding ground-glass
opacities are seen in posterior basal and medial basal segments of right lower lobe.
Patchy areas ground-glass opacities are seen in right middle lobe with a focal wedge
shaped area of subpleural consolidation in lateral segment of right middle lobe.
Suspicious filling defects are seen within subsegmental branches of right middle
Multiple enlarged upper and lower paratracheal, paraaortic and bilateral hilar lymph
nodes are seen, largest measuring 1.3 x1.3 cm in right hilar region.
The ascending aorta is prominent, measuring 4.3 cm in diameter.
Peripherally calcified nodule is seen in left lobe of thyroid.
The remaining pulmonary arterial branches are normal in caliber and contour.
The bones, muscles and subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.
